summary: M. R. Raghava Varier is an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He studied at the University of Calicut, the Archaeological Survey of India, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, later serving as Professor at the University of Calicut from around 1976 to 1996.

M. S. A. Rao studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. He held posts at the University of Delhi (1955-1985), the University of Pennsylvania (1968-1969), and Syracuse University.

M. Seshagiri Sastri was an Indologist and linguist. In 1899, he was attested as Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency College, Chennai, and as Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library.
M. Shinoda is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. Shinoda studied at Agoura High School, the Art Center College of Design, and under teacher Seiren Matsunami.

M. Yamunacharya was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Mysore Hiriyanna, Ardeshir Ruttonji Wadia, and Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. He served as Professor in Philosophy at Maharaja's College, Mysore.

Mabel Haynes Bode, a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, earned her PhD at the University of Bern under Edouard Müller-Hess and studied at UCL, Collège de France, Sorbonne, EPHE, and Pisa. She taught at UCL and SOAS (1917-1922).

Madeleine Biardeau was an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar. She studied at the École Normale Supérieure de Sèvres and the University of Kerala, and served as a teacher at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from around 1956 to 1989.
Madhav M. Deshpande is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ludo Rocher. He served as a professor at the University of Michigan, with posts attested in 1976 and from 2006 to 2009.
Madhu Khanna is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who held posts at Jamia Millia Islamia and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, both attested in 2012.

Madhusudan Amilal Dhaky was a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar who graduated from Fergusson College and founded the Archeology Research Group in 1951. He held leadership and research roles at the American Institute of Indian Studies from 1976 to 2016.

Maha Chakri Sirindhorn is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. She studied at Chitralada School, Chulalongkorn, Silpakorn (under Satya Vrat Shastri), Srinakharinwirot, Asian Institute of Technology, and Peking University.

Mahasi Sayadaw was a Buddhist and religious studies figure. He studied under traditional teachers including Mingun Jetawun Sayadaw U Narada, served as Abbot at Mawlamyine Monastery (1941) and teacher at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha, and founded Insight Meditation Society in 1979.
Mahesh A. Deokar is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He served at Savitribai Phule Pune University as Professor (attested 2011) and Head of department (attested 2020-2021).
Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya was an Indologist who studied under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University, attested in 1882 and 1914.

Mahinda Deegalle is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. Educated at Peradeniya, Harvard, and Chicago under Diana L. Eck, Frank E. Reynolds, and Wendy Doniger, he held posts at Harvard, McGill, Bath Spa University, and Colgate University.
Mahiro Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who serves as a professor at Bukkyo University, where he succeeded Norihiko Tanaka in 2021.
Maho Iuchi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD from Otani University by 2008 and was attested as a visiting researcher at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies in 2010.
Mai Mishiro is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011) and Waseda University (attested 2016).

Makio Takemura, a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, earned his degrees at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tokyo, Rissho, Mie, Tsukuba (1988-2002), and served as president of Toyo University from 2009 to 2020.

Makio Ueno is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Otani University in 2009 and later held positions there, including assistant professor attested from 2010 to 2012, and an attested post in 2022.
